Some observations about the "total" automation of software engineering:

1. There are more software engineers now than in 2025, and demand is growing.

2. Software engineers have never worked harder than they do now.

3. They largely don't write code anymore, agents write ~100% of the code.

4. The bottom line of the companies that employs these engineers and agents (i.e. the terminal purpose of all this code) is typically not budging as a result of AI adoption.

This is why you have to think in terms of systems. Automating one aspect of a system creates its own friction and moves the bottlenecks elsewhere.

Some impressions from the Bank-Fund meetings in Bangkok:

1. The words are all negative but the numbers are all positive. Is all about unprecedented waves of shocks and risks while the IMF upgraded the forecast to something even stronger.

2. No one cares about tariffs anymore, they expect them to continue forever and have adjusted and moved on.

3. Everyone cares a lot about high interest rates. They expect them to continue forever but they haven't moved on.

4. Oil prices fall somewhere between these two. Everyone cares some, aren't sure if they'll continue and have partially moved on.

5. Everyone is having exactly the same conversations about AI as they are having here: will the demand boost continue, is it a bubble, will it kill jobs, when will it show up in productivity. I sensed much more optimism than pessimism and finance ministers and central bankers are not particuarly interested in p(doom).

6. No one seemed to mind that Scott Bessent didn't bother to attend.

How many people in the world identify with a particular religion?

Religious compositions vary a lot from country to country.

In the United Kingdom, Christianity is the most popular, and following no religion is becoming increasingly common, particularly among young people. But it can be hard to get a sense of how these differences stack up globally.

The Pew Research Center publishes estimates of religious affiliation across the world. You can see the global breakdown in the chart for 2020 (the most recent year available). It shows the number of people who identify with each religion. Pew counts people by the religion they report, regardless of their beliefs or practices.

You can see that Christians are the largest group, with 2.3 billion people, followed by Muslims, with 2 billion. People with no religious affiliation come close behind.

Those not affiliated with any religion are among the largest groups in the world. But this undersells religion’s reach: when we add up all religious groups, most people in the world — around three in four — identify with a religion. Those with no religious affiliation are still a minority.

(written by @_HannahRitchie)

China wants to control AI exports. What does it mean for India? A quick FAQ.

Q: What happened?
China's commerce ministry, MOFCOM, released draft rules that put frontier AI under export controls. Model weights, source code, and training methods are covered.

Q: Which models are affected?
Models already released with open weights are not affected, because anything public is excluded. New releases, including new versions of existing models, are covered if they cross 10^26 training FLOPs, have 2 trillion parameters, or rank in the global top 10 on a major leaderboard, even a single category like coding. 

Models trained on China's "important data" are also covered, whatever their size. Models trained on "core data" cannot be exported at all.

Q: Will Chinese labs stop releasing open-weight models?
Probably not. Open-sourcing now counts as an "export," but restricted models can get an "automatic licence." Until the rules take effect, covered releases only have to be registered.

Q: So why should Indian builders care?
Many Indian startups fine-tune Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi. Those models now come out of a state-licensed pipeline. Beijing has said its support for open source is unchanged, but it now has a gate. Even a gate that stays open can be slowed or timed for a particular release.

Q: What about using Chinese models through APIs?
API and app access is not covered by these controls. 

Q: Anything else in the list?
Yes. AI agents, chip design at 14nm and below, 10,000-GPU cluster know-how, and AI cyber tools are all restricted. 

China is now treating its AI stack as strategic leverage, the way the US treats chips.

Q: The lesson for India?
We had written earlier that China will start controlling open weight models before Dec 2028. Both the US and China now see frontier AI as something to control. We need multiple options including our own. Other open weight models like Mistral from France get a foot in the door.

Q: What should we watch?
How long licences take for major releases, and if top Chinese models start slipping their release dates. Delays would show up long before any outright denial.

Simplifying in silico protein evolution with minimal screening by unZipro

1. Qin et al. introduce unZipro, a geometric deep learning framework for zero-shot protein evolution that aims to cut experimental screening down to “top ~10” candidates while still finding high-fitness variants across diverse protein families.

2. Core idea: start with a compact structure-based inverse folding model (GNN encoder–decoder) pre-trained on 24,501 non-redundant single-chain protein structures to learn general sequence–structure constraints, then adapt it to a target protein family via homolog-guided meta-learning.

3. The “family-specific expert” concept is central: meta-transfer learning (MAML) plus homologous structures retrieved by Foldseek is used to shift a generalist inverse folding model toward a family-specific fitness landscape without using task-specific experimental labels.

4. Benchmarking on ProteinGym (217 DMS datasets; 2.46M mutations): meta-learning improves average Spearman correlation from 0.3703 (pre-trained) to 0.4163 (12.4% relative gain). unZipro outperforms several inverse-folding baselines and reaches performance comparable to large PLM-based inverse folding approaches, despite fewer parameters and less training data.

5. Practical engineering claim: unZipro prioritizes beneficial mutations with minimal wet-lab testing. Across nine protein engineering tasks, testing fewer than ten nominated variants yields an average success rate of 61% for high-fitness hits, supporting a low-screening design-build-test loop.

6. Gene editing improvements in crops are a major emphasis: for TadA8e (ABE), fine-tuned unZipro nominates 6 candidates and identifies 4 high-fitness variants (66.6% hit rate). The TadA8e T83N variant improves A-to-G editing (up to ~1.9-fold in reporter assays), boosts endogenous wheat editing across loci, and reduces genome-wide off-target A-to-G substitutions in WGS.

7. Nuclease optimization: for SpCas9, unZipro nominates 20 candidates; several improve editing, with D1180G reaching up to 12.8-fold higher Indels at a wheat target site, and no detected increase in genome-wide mutational burden or off-target edits (WGS + candidate-site checks).

8. Hypercompact CasΦ2 is upgraded further by combining unZipro-designed variants with a T5 exonuclease fusion strategy. The T5E(Y58F)-CasΦ2(Y356F) fusion yields 1.8- to 27.9-fold increases over CasΦ2 across wheat loci (up to 85% Indels at one site), and the headline result reports up to 28-fold gain for T5E-CasΦ2 fusion variants.

9. Prime editing: unZipro leverages two structural states of the PE complex (initiation vs elongation) to nominate MMLV-RT mutations; 70% (7/10) and 86.7% (13/15) of tested mutations improve PEmax activity in wheat protoplast reporters. A rational combination strategy (structure + conformational state + co-evolutionary coupling) yields PEmax(R253K/T246H), named PEUltra, with up to 2.2-fold improvement over ePPEplus at endogenous wheat sites and high efficiency in transgenics.

10. Beyond editors, unZipro is shown on non-enzymes and plant proteins using AlphaFold3 structures: firefly luciferase activity is improved (e.g., M164I gives ~4.1-fold); rice TFs (OsPHR2, OsNAC3) show high hit rates for enhanced transcriptional activation; and barley methionine synthase HvMS1 variants increase methionine and confer stronger broad-spectrum antiviral effects against both PVX (RNA virus) and BSCTV (DNA virus) in Nicotiana benthamiana.

中国的人口变局 👶🏻👴🏻

1949 年之后，中国有过三波婴儿潮，每一波婴儿长大成人，都要吃饭穿衣和就业。

第一波在建国后的头十年。

这拨人成年时，城市吸纳不了这么多年轻人，文革又停了高考和招工，最后靠上山下乡，把城市的就业压力转移到了农村。

第二波从 60 年代初到 70 年代中期，出生规模最大。

他们成年时赶上了改革开放，个体户、乡镇企业和沿海工厂接住了大部分人。但这代人，也是后来下岗潮的主角。

第三波80/90后，是第二波60后的儿女。

他们赶上了大学扩招、城市化和中国入世，好日子很大程度上来自融入全球化。有了全球化，广大中西部的青年人，才有机会南下进厂，为全世界生产衣帽鞋袜，换取微薄的收入，来满足吃饭穿衣的需求。

2022 年起，中国再次迎来人口变局，可这次不是变多，而是变少。更诡异的是，出生人口和就业机会都在变少，唯独需要赡养的老人在变多，属于两头挤压。

至于就业机会为啥减少，原因并不复杂，全球化退潮，中美、中欧、中日相继出现贸易摩擦，而中国经济也因为泡沫破裂，进入了低增长时代。有人说这是人口过剩，其实真正的矛盾，就是失业率高企叠加深度老龄化。

不难发现，中国人下乡还是进厂，做鞋袜还是做芯片，从来都是人口变局倒逼现实政治的结果。

换句话说，人口就像燃料，用来推动经济还是引爆社会，关键就看政治体制能否及时反应，能不能把人口压力转化为经济动力。

所以问题来了，前三波人口变局，都有一次政策转向来承接，那么这一次又当如何呢？
